data.label: Receive Customer Issue
data.description: A customer issue is submitted or arrives through a support channel and starts the workflow.
data.rationale: This is a deterministic trigger event: the workflow starts when a support ticket, message, or case arrives. No AI, ML, or language understanding is required beyond basic channel intake and event detection, so L0 is sufficient.

data.label: Triage Issue
data.description: Review the incoming issue to understand its general nature, urgency, and required handling path.
data.rationale: Triage can often be handled with deterministic rules, but the description implies interpreting the issue's general nature and urgency from customer input, which typically needs language understanding. L2 is appropriate because the step is mainly classifying and extracting meaning from text rather than generating responses. L0 was considered first, but variation in customer phrasing makes pure rules less reliable.

data.label: Gather Customer Details
data.description: Collect missing information from the customer needed to fully understand the issue.
data.rationale: This step usually requires generating a follow-up message or prompting the customer for missing fields. That moves it beyond L2 because it must draft natural language tailored to the gap in information. A single LLM agent is enough; no external tools or multi-agent collaboration are required.

data.label: Classify Customer Need
data.description: Determine what the customer actually needs, such as support, correction, replacement, or escalation.
data.rationale: This is a text classification / intent categorization task. It can be implemented with NLU or a supervised classifier that maps issue text to categories like support, refund, replacement, or escalation. L0 is insufficient because customer phrasing varies widely, but no generative output is required.

data.label: Resolve Issue Directly
data.description: Handle the issue using standard support actions when it can be solved without escalation.
data.rationale: If the step means applying predefined support actions such as issuing a known fix, updating a record, or executing a standard policy path, it is deterministic. L0 is enough because the workflow already routes here only when the issue matches a standard resolution path. No AI is needed for the action itself.

data.label: Escalate Issue
data.description: Route the issue to a specialist, manager, or other team when it cannot be resolved at the current level.
data.rationale: Escalation is a deterministic routing step: if predefined conditions indicate the issue needs a specialist, the case is reassigned or forwarded. This is standard workflow automation and does not require AI.

data.label: Take Corrective Action
data.description: Apply the appropriate corrective action to address the customer’s problem and move it toward resolution.
data.rationale: The node is described as applying the appropriate corrective action, which can be implemented as a rule-based action map once the issue type is known. Since upstream classification and escalation already determine the path, the actual corrective action is likely a deterministic workflow operation. L0 is sufficient unless hidden complexity requires dynamic reasoning.

data.label: Verify Resolution
data.description: Confirm that the issue has been resolved and that the customer’s need has been satisfied.
data.rationale: Verification often involves interpreting customer confirmation, support notes, or follow-up responses to determine whether the issue is truly resolved. That requires language understanding and possibly sentiment or status classification. It does not require generation, so L2 is the best fit.

data.label: Request More Information
data.description: If the issue is not resolved or the outcome is unclear, ask the customer for additional details or clarification.
data.rationale: This step must generate a customer-facing follow-up asking for missing or unclear information. That is a natural language generation task, which exceeds L2. A single LLM call can draft the request; no tools or multi-agent orchestration are necessary.

data.label: Close Case
data.description: Record the resolution, finalize the ticket or case, and end the workflow.
data.rationale: Closing a case is a deterministic end-of-workflow operation: update status, store resolution metadata, and terminate the process. This is classic rule-based automation with no AI requirement.

data.condition: issue can be solved without escalation
data.label: if standard resolution applies

data.condition: issue needs more information or further action
data.label: if unresolved

message: This workflow is mostly deterministic support automation with a few language-understanding and generation touchpoints. Classification and verification rely on L2, while customer-facing follow-up messages require L3. The remainder of the flow is L0 routing and case-management logic. No multi-agent orchestration is needed.
